subject: invention/pigeon-post
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset: one invention-card sketch for a historical atlas.
One landscape 3:2 page from an explorers field sketchbook. Visible loose graphite construction lines, quick sepia ink and parallel hatching, restrained uneven watercolour washes in ochre, grey-green and faded blue. Detail concentrated on the principal object or action; outer edges dissolve irregularly into warm cream paper with subtle foxing. An observed working sketch, not a polished painting, digital render, photograph, infographic or collage. A single coherent principal scene, optionally one small unlabelled detail study. No frame, binding, captions, labels, signature, watermark or readable writing. Any marks on historic artifacts remain small and nonverbal. People, materials and tools appropriate to the place and date.
Scene: Close view of a Mamluk pigeon keeper's hands gently holding a natural grey homing pigeon beside a small rolled message being attached to its leg, on a Cairo rooftop around1270. Low pigeon-loft openings and restrained medieval Cairo roofscape recede into soft wash. Simple long tunic and wrapped headcloth, no foreground sultan. Tiny paper note, no oversized scroll, modern plastic leg band or later Ottoman skyline.
Keep machinery, hands, hulls and load-bearing parts geometrically coherent. Use a distinct observational viewpoint as specified. No text, captions or labels anywhere; historical writing may only appear as tiny indistinct marks.
